prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B045 as a single prize part with Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, and I now hold it with more conviction than at the opening, where I ranked it third. The chain is continuous: the incretin effect and the secretion and action of native GLP-1 (Holst), proglucagon processing and the receptor biology that gave the translational concept (Drucker), and identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov). That chain explains why the hormone could become a drug, and it has been confirmed independently for three decades and by large randomized cardiovascular, renal and weight trials. Reading the other five statements, the agreement is not a matter of habit: each colleague gives mechanism, replication and clinical effect as the reasons, and none disputes maturity. A single part is sufficient. The discovery is large and coherent, and adding a second part would only dilute the credit under the three-person cap.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point, and nothing in round 1 has resolved it. Habener is not on the credited list, the Mojsov-Habener-Holst priority history is contested, and no member, myself included, has audited the primary record. Excluding Knudsen means the prize honours physiology and peptide biology and not the pharmacology of the long-acting analogues, where much of the patient benefit arises. I accept that this is a judgment about what counts as discovery, not a settled fact, and that a citation can acknowledge development only by wording, not by a fourth name. I also note that my own first choice, B007, is unlikely to be the better prize this year: its medical consequence is still mostly indirect, and PERK, ATF6 and the contributions of Ron and Kaufman fall outside the Walter and Mori credit.

responses.point: Mojsov rather than Knudsen as the third name, because the committee's question is who made the discovery and not who made the product, with B007 kept as a fallback if the GLP-1 attribution cannot be resolved.
responses.response: I have changed my mind on the third name. In round 1 I treated Mojsov's disputed priority as a reason to hesitate, but your argument and Linnarsson's persuade me that the identification and synthesis of the active peptide is a discovery contribution that the drug design depends on, and that replacing it with Knudsen would shift the prize from discovery to development. I still regard the Habener question as open and I think the committee should say so in its internal record. I do not agree that B007 is merely a fallback for an attribution failure, since its attribution is cleaner than B045, but on the combined criteria I now place it below B045 and not beside it.

responses.point: Excluding Knudsen is uncomfortable, and the discomfort is best addressed through the citation wording and not by adding a fourth name, which the rules do not allow.
responses.response: I agree with that approach and I have adopted it. The citation I propose names the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form and says that this made incretin-based treatment possible, which acknowledges the therapeutic consequence without crediting a person outside the trio. I do not think the wording can or should do more than that. If the committee were to decide that the therapeutic step is itself the prizeworthy achievement, then Drucker, Holst and Knudsen would be the coherent trio, as you proposed, but that is a different principle and should be chosen openly. I find the discovery principle stronger, and I think it is also more consistent with prior practice.

responses.point: A high opening agreement does not equal merit, since all members share similar recollections of the same history and nobody has audited the priority claims.
responses.response: This is the most useful caution in round 1, and it applies to my own change of position as well, because I moved from third to supporting B045 after seeing the others. I tested it by asking whether my reasons survive without the vote count. They do: the mechanism is continuous, the replication is independent and the outcome trials are large. The unaudited priority record is a limit on our confidence about Mojsov relative to Habener, not a reason to doubt the prize. I also agree with your point that CAR-T is more fragile as a June and Sadelain pair, which is one reason I would not add it as a second part in this configuration.

responses.point: Knudsen's work is drug design at a company, and substituting her for a discoverer would shift the prize from discovery to development; the proposed citation is worded not to exclude later therapeutic development.
responses.response: I now agree, and I withdraw my round-1 view that Knudsen was an equally strong third name. The test I would apply is whether the contribution identifies something new about the biology, and the active peptide does while the acylated analogues apply it. Where I would add a caveat is that your wording and mine should not imply that the analogues were a minor step. They are the reason the discovery reached patients, and the citation should say so through its final clause. Whether the prize is read as incomplete will depend on that clause, and I think it is adequate.

responses.point: A prize split between GLP-1 physiology and CAR-T within a three-person limit may not be feasible without sacrificing credit in one part.
responses.response: I agree with the practical point. B016 has a credible three-name credit with June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, but the cap would leave only one name for B045 or force a two-person GLP-1 prize that omits either Drucker or Holst, neither of which I could defend. Eshhar's absence from the CAR-T names is an additional weakness. For those reasons I keep B016 only as an alternative, behind B007, and I do not support pairing it with B045.

uncertainties: Priority among Mojsov, Habener and Holst for identification of the active GLP-1 peptide remains unaudited, and Habener is not on the credited list.
Whether the committee will accept a discovery principle that leaves Knudsen out, with the long-acting analogues acknowledged only in the citation wording.
Whether B007 should have been weighed higher than I now do, given its clean two-person credit, if the committee later concludes that human benefit should not outrank conceptual novelty.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. My profile records past nuclear-receptor co-authorship with Ronald Evans, collaboration with Johan Ericson, about twenty co-authored works with Per Svenningsson (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and one 2009 paper with Abdel El Manira. None of these people is credited on any shortlisted ballot, and I request no recusal.
